auxiliary_material: The authors cite preclinical mechanisms in the background and discussion, including inosine's role in inhibiting UBA6 to increase tumor immunogenicity, serving as a carbon source for CD8+ T cells, and activating IFN-γ/TNF-α pathways. The study design is a single-center, prospective, randomized, open-label Phase 2 trial registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05809336). The dosage regimen and safety data support the feasibility of repurposing inosine as an adjunct therapy.
outline_action: Search for pharmacokinetic or metabolomic studies that specifically quantify baseline inosine levels in human tumor biopsies or plasma prior to immunotherapy initiation. Look for correlative analyses linking these endogenous measurements to clinical response (ORR/PFS/OS) without exogenous intervention. Consider reviewing studies that utilize mass spectrometry on paired tumor-normal tissue samples to establish physiological ranges.
remaining_gap: This study does not measure or report the absolute physiological concentration of inosine within the human tumor microenvironment (TME) or interstitial fluid. It evaluates the efficacy of administered supplementation rather than correlating baseline endogenous inosine levels with treatment outcomes. Consequently, the specific data regarding natural TME inosine concentrations and their statistical association with ICI efficacy (independent of supplementation) remain unavailable from this material.
useful_material: This study provides clinical evidence that exogenous inosine supplementation (0.2 g, three times/day) combined with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors significantly prolongs progression-free survival (median 7.00 months vs. 4.40 months; HR 0.63) compared to inhibitors alone in 172 patients with advanced solid tumors. It reports a trend toward improved objective response rate (26.7% vs. 15.1%) and an acceptable safety profile with reduced Grade 3-4 adverse reactions in the inosine group. Subgroup analyses indicate stronger PFS benefits in lung cancer patients and those with specific baseline inflammatory markers (e.g., low PLR/NLR).
